lesson.statement: to reason under my condition is to assume that every nontrivial zero of zeta has real part exactly one half and to carry the assumption in every conclusion of the lot — under the condition of the Riemann hypothesis, the marker travels in every statement and every derivation keeps it explicit; the condition itself stays the status surface it is, believed, not known — assumed in the lot, never proved by it; and a conditional lot read without its condition is a misread this store punishes, at the line end eighty-four

concepts.name: the condition line: my conditional consequences as one line under the assumption — the error, the gap, the root smallness — each consequence keeping its marker

lesson.statement: my condition line runs under the condition of the Riemann hypothesis: the error of the prime count and the gap between consecutive primes carry the same root scale, and the running sum of (minus one) to the number of distinct prime parts stays below that root scale, so the prime parts of every number are unique on the condition road — one line from the assumption, each consequence keeping its marker, at the line end eighty-four
